title: Egress broker and subnet-tiling for endpoint mapping and upgrade-safe routing
creator: Aisha N'diaye
description: Design and implement a reusable Terraform module (egress-broker) to manage VPC subnet classes, NAT/IGW placement, VPC endpoints, and route table mappings with upgrade-safe migration hooks and runtime health checks. Module should support: (1) deterministic subnet tiling across AZs, (2) pluggable egress profiles (NAT gateway per-az, shared NAT fleet, or customer-managed IGW), (3) centralized VPC endpoint creation with least-privilege endpoint policies, (4) route table orchestration with canary migration plan, and (5) builtin synthetic health checks and reconciler that surface drift in endpoint connectivity and NAT capacity. Target consumers: Private deployment onboarding teams and Dedicated capacity infra stacks.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes variables for subnet_class (control_plane, worker, egress), cidr_sizing, az_distribution, and egress_profile and applies without manual steps
Module can create VPC Endpoints (S3, ECR, SSM, KMS) with generated endpoint policies when 'managed_endpoints' is true
Route tables are created and tagged consistently; changing egress_profile triggers a canary plan that provisions new route table and attaches to 1 AZ for 24h before full cutover
Synthetic health checks run as part of apply (via null_resource/provisioner or external operator) and must confirm: endpoint reachable, NAT has available elastic IPs, route propagation is correct
Upgrade plan includes safe-state hooks: pre-checks (schema drift), staged apply, post-apply validation, and automatic rollback instruction notes in plan output
Module supports outputs that can be consumed by downstream modules: private_subnet_ids, egress_subnet_ids, endpoint_ids, route_table_ids
Documentation and example usage exist in repo/examples/private_vpc/ with terraform 1.5+ and provider versions pinned
Automated acceptance test (CI) runs a plan+apply in a disposable account and validates health checks and route attachments (green on merge)
implementation_notes: Use Terraform 1.5 and AWS provider >= 5.0 to leverage 'for_each' on subnets and improved provider lifecycle
Subnet tiling algorithm: deterministic hash of vpc_id + az + subnet_class -> ip math to produce non-overlapping /24 blocks per AZ; allow explicit overrides
For canary migrations, create parallel route_table_<canary> and route_table_<primary>; attach canary to a single AZ via route table association; add a 'canary_ttl_hours' var default 24
Health checks implemented as provisioned Lambda invoked from Terraform via local-exec or external data source depending on target environment; prefer external operator in private/on-premified setups
Endpoint policies should be generated from a template with allow-list of principal actions; expose 'endpoint_policy_overrides' for security teams
Avoid inline PEMs or secrets in module; rely on KMS key ARNs passed in for encrypted resources and document KMS rotation constraints
Module must emit structured tags for cost center, environment, project, and 'redwood:module' metadata for inventory
State locking: document remote state backend requirements (S3 backend with DynamoDB lock) and recommend workspace per-deployment pattern
test_plan: Unit: terraform validate and tflint in CI on all module changes
Integration: terraform plan+apply in ephemeral AWS account -> run synthetic checks: curl metadata endpoint via VPC endpoint, S3 put/get via endpoint, NAT egress to external IP
Canary test: simulate egress_profile change from 'per_az_nat' to 'shared_nat_autoscale' and assert only canary AZ's routing changes during canary_ttl
Upgrade test: run module upgrade path with older state file to ensure lifecycle blocks do not destroy/recreate healthy subnets; validate outputs remain stable
Chaos test: simulate NAT gateway deletion externally and assert module health check surfaces alert and creates remediation ticket stub
Regression: ensure no implicit dependency on account-level resources; support explicit provider_alias for accounts in different partitions
risk_mitigation: Potential issue: provider destroys routes on replace. Mitigation: use create_before_destroy where safe and lifecycle ignore_changes for tags/stateful attrs
Potential issue: insufficient EIP quota. Mitigation: detect quota in pre-check and fall back to shared_nat_autoscale or fail fast with clear remediation
Potential issue: endpoint policy overly permissive. Mitigation: default to deny-all template and require security approval to widen access
Potential issue: Terraform long-running applies for large infra. Mitigation: limit changes per apply via canary toggles and staged CI jobs
Potential issue: drift between terraform and operator reconciler. Mitigation: document precedence and provide read-only operator mode plus drift-reporting in console
